reviews.title: A truly unique dining experience you won’t want to pass up while you’re enjoying your stay in Lima, Peru.
reviews.text: My husband and I enjoy trying local cuisine and new experiences with dining options. Well this place is certainly one of those places. The menu is thoughtful and exciting but not overly daring. The food is Peruvian but with international influences. And yet they offer a classic flan that I swear is the BEST you’ll ever have!!! The ambience is great for a couple or small group in this quaint setting. The experience will be unforgettable for sure!!

reviews.title: Outstanding
reviews.text: The food was sublime. Truly outstanding technique and flavor combinations. The setting was demure and relaxing cannot recommend enough

reviews.title: Highly enjoyable
reviews.text: We had a excellent lunch experience. After eating two tasting menus in a row, we switched to à la cart in the morning. We are super grateful for that. We’re also thankful that the staff was so easy to accommodate us. The à la carte menu has a lot of different options. The waitress was able to make recommendations on what we should order. The scallops with sankey is definitely a must have. I probably could’ve eaten another couple of those. It was so light and refreshing. The Popeye crab was also very interesting with almost thai flavors, very balanced. The fish curry was cooked perfectly. The different flavors mixed with the pani puri bread was super fun. The rice with squid was also very well thought out. The fresh peas added the texture that it needed. It was a homey and very thoughtful dish. Thankfully, we received room for dessert. The flan is the best flan I’ve ever had in my entire life. The custard was luxurious and luscious on the tongue. Definitely a highlight. The grilled custard apple with such an interesting dish. It was fun to eat and had a great almost pancake toast on the bottom, topped with a grilled custard, apple, topped with a crisp of the custard apple. On the side, there was almost this goat cheese/funky ice cream, which really complimented everything. It was by far one of the most interesting and flavorful dishes.

reviews.title: What creativity, how rich!
reviews.text: Vow! I love creativity, flavors and service! Definitely inside the top top of Lima! From now on if on my visit list to Lima!

great experience and special food we never heard of.

reviews.title: This place is superb even though it was recommended by Giles Coren!
reviews.text: Situated in a central side street in Barranco this is a delight to visit. There is a tasting menu which looked substantial so we went with the a la carte. This grilled scallops were two perfect mouthfuls, the sweetbreads- the best I have ever had, the lamb could be but with a spoon and the belly pork perfect. The servers were engaging and not imposing. Exceptional value my best meals in Peru. Suits a Western palate well

reviews.title: Best meal of my life
reviews.text: Without a doubt the best meal of my life.  I do not say that lightly as I live in New Orleans and have been to many fabulous restaurants there.  I also have lived in Philly and travel so have had the privilege to try many restaurants other places.  Flavors were out of this world and the combinations of food, flavor, and texture was outstanding.  We also did the South American wine pairing which was the perfect compliment to every course.  Staff were the ultimate professionals.  This in itself would have made for the most memorable night on our trip, but when we struggled to catch an uber due to no international cell service plus construction in the area Chef Martinez himself came out to help us, walked 2 blocks with us, and only left once we got into the car.  So not only is he one of the best chefs in the world but a kind and helpful man at his core.  If you travel to Lima your trip will not be complete without a stop at Merito.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: Best meal in Lima, hands down. I unfortunately did not do many other fine dining or highly acclaimed restaurants during my trip, but Merito exceeded already high expectations. Each dish was an adventure: beautifully presented and all tastes amazing. Some dishes surprised me with textures and flavors. The service was attentive and very professional. The cocktails were fantastic. Ambience and music very tasteful. Price is amazing for what you get. Highly recommended

reviews.title: Amazing experience
reviews.text: This is an amazing experience and journey through creation and flavours! Just amazing. We set at the kitchen counter and watched art with culinary come together!

reviews.title: I would give it a Michelin star
reviews.text: This was one of the most amazing lunches I ever had to be able to combine delicious and beautiful food and healthy. All at once is truly an art on top of being very fast as well. I didn’t want it to end. Wish I had somebody there with me so I can taste more of their menu. It’s just so much you could eat when you’re by yourself. It was a very buried special restaurant coming from a person that ate all over the world truly amazing not recommended for the backpacker budget

reviews.title: Merito a great fusion food experience
reviews.text: Merito was an excellent experience in fusion food. The atmosphere was casual. The wait staff were excellent. They explained each dish. Gave recommendations and were there to answer any questions. I would highly recommend Merito. The food presentation was unique and food was delicious.

reviews.title: Acidity
reviews.text:
I start from food: as per the title, acidity. Nothing more. Each dish had a constant, this acidity foretold so much that, at the end of the ten courses, it was all so obvious in taste that boredom had taken over. Every single dish ended with this sour tone and all this was repeated again and again. 

Atmosphere: Medium/high music and very loud cold air conditioning made the room uncomfortable. Beautiful lighting. 

Service: our table was tied, for service, to another table, so, if we had not yet finished the other table had to wait and vice versa. In addition, we were served by 4 different waiters who could not explain the ingredients used (except superficially) while the explanation of the ingredients was supposed to be the main focus of this experience. 

Disappointment is so much also because it seems to enter a temple of cuisine and everything tries to be so perfect that then at the end of dinner you do not have much left except, precisely, this immense disappointment. The price is high, the disappointment more!

reviews.title: Fantastic, amazing, sensational….I could go on.
reviews.text:
This was bought as a 40th wedding anniversary gift by our 3 adult kids as they knew that we were coming to Peru and our son had eaten there a few years before.
The building is unusual in that you walk through the kitchen with a chefs table and taken upstairs to the restaurant itself. It does have the industrial vibe with bare bricks etc but our table and chairs were comfortable. We were having the 10 course tasting menu and the staff were very attentive to my allergen request of no onions. 
Each course was fantastic with Peruvian ingredients the majority we had never heard of. The flavours were amazing as well as having playful variations in texture and colours. Each course was explained by the staff with advice how to eat it to get the most out of each course.
By the sixth course I was feeling full and was worrying whether I would be able to finish the menu but the chef’s playfulness came into its own and I finished the meal just right.
We had a bottle of Albariño which complemented the food. 

The meal was simply stunning on all levels and entered my top 10 meals eaten out and we have eaten in quite a few Michelin star restaurants including Arzak, Gordon Ramseys and L’Enclume and is was as good as them.

Sat near us was an American guy sat by himself having the same menu taking photos.
We met him outside and had a quick chat about the meal. He had visited a  world renowned restaurant around the corner and said this meal was one third of the price and twice as good- I think that summed up the whole experience for us.

reviews.title: Exquisite Flavors & Outstanding Service at Merito
reviews.text: Merito is a must-visit in Lima! The food is exquisite-each dish bursting with flavor and beautifully presented. The service was top-notch, and the staff’s recommendations were spot on. The chefs went above and beyond by customizing non-veg dishes into delicious vegetarian options. A perfect blend of creativity, taste, and warm hospitality. 💖

reviews.title: It has its merit
reviews.text:
Excellent care, although I was left with the doubt it is necessary so much staff.
Almost a waiter per diner 🙃. 

Very tasty food.

reviews.title: Sensational dinner!!
reviews.text:
We had looked forward to our trip to Merito for several months and once we’d arrived in Peru , our anticipation grew as we found the incredible level of respect found across the whole country for ingredients. Peru is not known as the garden of South America for nothing, with the variety of ecosystems that support multitudes of flora & fauna.

 Chef Juan Luis Martinez, graciously allowed us to take our tasting menu at the bar in the kitchen and watching the team at work in their creation of the dishes that we were to consume was a fantastic experience. A menu that takes modern and classic cooking techniques with a laser like focus on ingredients. You’re hard put to find a superfluous ingredient on a plate here. Everything has a place and a reason for its inclusion.

We both took the tasting menu, a representation of around 10 courses that take you on a journey inspired both by the chef’s Venezuelan heritage in addition to the Peruvian backscape of ingredients available. The Coast, the Amazon & The Andes provided Swordfish. Crab, Scallops and Lobster, Paiche ( a large freshwater fish) and young Goat for us together with a selection of tubers, quinoas and vegetables some of which I had never come across previously, to create a menu which  represented the best of Peru & Venezuela  in both technique and combination. The light smoke given to most dishes by virtue of the carob tree wood glowing in the oven gave a light but intense addition to dishes which was well received. I also took the Wine pairing to accompany the menu, a voyage which took us all over South America from Peru to Uruguay to Argentina & Chile with wines that were challenging but never to the point of disrupting the balance and harmony with their accompanying dishes. Often small or even micro producers. The wine pairing had obviously been considered at length and much like the menu everything had a reason & rationale for being there.

This was an epic journey and whilst one might easily think that this was entirely led by the dishes presented. Our waiter with his intimate knowledge of the dishes meant that rather than just reeling off a list of ingredients (as is often found in good restaurants) we were given deep descriptions of cooking techniques, sourcing of ingredients and more which gave a significantly deeper understanding and thus enjoyment of everything we ate. Supplemented by the Sommeliers previously noted excellent wine choices and informative descriptions, made for a more than excellent evening. Merito provides excellent value for a restaurant of its calibre but do not mistake value for any loss of quality. From someone who has been fortunate enough to visit a significant number of Michelin starred and highly rated restaurants, The gastronomic journey to be found at Merito is one of the best!

reviews.title: One of the Best New Restaurants in Peru
reviews.text:
Former Central chef.  Excellent a la carte Venezuelan Peruvian cuisine. Loved the food here.  Lunch or dinner.  Has a walk in kitchen counter also. 

Service: impeccable and friendly.  English speaking staff.

reviews.title: Amazing place
reviews.text:
What a great experience! We were visiting Lima for a few days  post a tour of Peru! We love good food. We were not disappointed. The restaurant is located in the trendy area, Barranco. The restaurant is humble and minimalist in its decor with a ‘cool’ relaxing vibe. The staff greeted us warmly and were super helpful about the menu and drinks. We had the following and loved everything:

Pez & Kiwicha
Mamet & Cangrejo popeye
Conchas, Sandi & Jalapeño
Choclo al la brasa
Cabrita & Tuberculos
El Flan
Roca 

The quality and presentation was high and the incredible flavour combinations. The recommended wine by the sommelier was perfect. (Vigo carignan). So glad we could visit. Highly recommended.

reviews.title: Great interesting restaurant with local ingredients.
reviews.text: We were lucky to get a seat at the bar without a reservation. The bar seats were not super comfortable but the service, food and atmosphere were so good that we didn't care all that much. The drink service was interesting with unusual and well-crafted cocktails and a nice selection of wines. There were also interesting non-alcoholic drinks. We had two appetizers, one was a remarkable concoction with different types of corn that was incredibly complex and delicious, the other was scallops with sanki and jalapeno that were super fresh and perfect. We had pork belly, perfectly cooked and served with puffy arepas to stuff it into along with a couple of sauces and lightly pickled cabbage. and we had the fish of the day; a pacific white fish that was perfectly cooked and came with a delicious Peruvian black mint sauce. The chocolate rock and the, if I remeber correctly, Cherimoya cherimoya cherimoya - three varieties of dessert featuring the fruit, were both superb. I'm not sure how much good knowing what we ate will do you; the menu changes frequently. I am looking forward to going back.

reviews.title: A mixed experience
reviews.text:
The positives:
The room is lovely, with a bit of an industrial vibe. 
The food is beautiful presented. 
Service is attentive.

The not so good:
The air con fans spew very cold air on your neck, suffered from a headache the entire day after (no, I didn’t drink too much). 
Some of the sauces with the main courses are way too salty. At a certain point I couldn’t even taste the nuances of the dishes, all I could taste was salt. 
No real vegetables in the dishes. 
Reading the menu it’s a bit hard to gauge how large the portions may be, making it difficult to know how much to order. 
A couple of dishes weren’t described properly by the server, ended up ordering a frozen dessert concoction when I was already cold, just because the words “cold” or “frozen” were never used.

reviews.title: WINE PRICES
reviews.text:
The food was delicious. Octopus, gizzards, fish... I ate better but rich, nothing to say.
But wines, really, too expensive for quality. 
An intikalpa, s/150 when you find s/32 in wong... no.

reviews.title: One of the best meals of our life
reviews.text: Great tasty innovative food. One of the top 5 meals of our lives. Food was not only visually amazing but tasty as well. The flan is amazing. Make your reservations early - it is a small restaurant. Service is amazing - one of the servers noticed we were hesitating on the sidewalk after dinner - our Uber had pulled up across the street - he came out and stopped traffic for us and escorted us over to the Uber - amazing.

reviews.title: Meal with a lot of potential
reviews.text:
My husband and I visited Merito for a lunch date.

It was the last of the top 50 restaurants in the world located in Lima we were yet to try and expectations were high.

The restaurant is located in a traditional shop in Barranco, just around the corner from Central and Kjolle.

The entrance is through the open kitchen and then you get promptly taken to the table upstairs.

There are two rooms with 6 tables each (quite close to each other). The style is smart casual and the crowd is very trendy.

We opted for a selection of dishes which we shared, accompanied by wine (there is no matching, you pick wine by glass or go for a bottle).

We thought that Scallops, sanki and jalapeños & white fish with cocoa fruit were good,  octopus, fish curry and arepas were fantastic and so was flan (one of the best I’ve ever had). Coconut dessert was average and so was the wine selection by glass.

Overall we had a nice afternoon, ate well and thought it was value for money (£170 for two, including 3 glasses of wine each & teas and coffees)

reviews.title: Young Restaurant
reviews.text: * Merit - located in the “young” neighborhood called “barrancas” the merit offers a tapas style menu. Small dishes to divide. We ordered the corn, the popai crab, and the entrance caterpillars. Tasty, but nothing spectacular. The crab, in particular, had a strange taste. The best are the main dishes, highlighting the pork and the curry’ fish that were great. It is among the 7 best in Latin America according to expert critics. Price below the average of the others. It is worth going there and dps go pro bar Ayuhasca, which is in the same neighborhood. Ps: bons drinks

reviews.title: creative & outstanding food and cocktails, beautiful ambiance and top-notch service
reviews.text:
I loved everything about our dinner at Merito. The ambiance and music are relaxed and chic, and my husband and I were blown away by the food. 

The crackers with Andean grains and white fish and the seafood curry were outstanding, and we had a ceviche with a fruit we've never tried before that was excellent. If you are a pescatarian or a fan of fresh fish you must try Merito! The value is also excellent-we didn't pay much more than we would for a standard dinner out in NYC and everything about our experience was exceptional. 

I had an excellent cocktail with coconut and cardamom. The N/A cocktail options were also sophisticated and the one my husband ordered was delicious. 

The service is also top-notch. Alexandra was especially helpful and patient answering our many questions and gently offering recommendations. 

Even among the countless excellent dining options in Lima I would absolutely go back to Merito, and I will be dreaming out it until then!

reviews.title: What an incredible experience!
reviews.text: Feels like fine dining but in a relaxed, casual setting. Instead of a tasting menu, you can choose from a variety of dishes on the menu. The staff was attentive and so helpful with recommendations. Everything we tried was outstanding. Our top picks are the fish curry, which we almost skipped but were convinced to order by wait staff—we were blown away. And the flan is TO DIE FOR! Merito is a must-visit!

reviews.title: Amazing !!!
reviews.text:
Beautiful food presentation, exquisite food served on simple plates. Service was quiet and discreet and wine recommendations were perfect. 
Totally Gluten Free friendly - I was able to share all of the plates that we the family chose together, which is unusual. 
The little starters, crab, fresh fish and mix of local fruits and vegetables were delicious. The lamb and tubers, catch of the day and pork dish with small corn like pitta breads were excellent. I cannot recommend this wonderful restaurant experience enough. The corn and coffee desert was like nothing we have ever tried and was just delicious.

reviews.title: Go there

reviews.title: Great
reviews.text: An excellent experience. Merit has a more intimate atmosphere, with excellent execution. The food was sensational, the best I've ever eaten in my life. I also liked the service.

reviews.title: Simply fantastic!
reviews.text: Excellence needs few words. Fantastic food. Small and refined place without being pretentious. The same can be said for the service. It's worth the whole price.

reviews.title: Amazing food and poor service!
reviews.text:
The food without words is sensational,
Congratulations to the Chefs, everything is delicious. Service is confusing and poor. I asked the waiter about the orange wine and he told me that it was a natural wine and that I wasn't used to it. (Apparently he knows me and knows what I drink). I asked for water and they brought imported water (one thing that really irritates me is paying more for water, the tables with foreigners serve imported water and the local tables serve national water). The restaurant is no longer cheap, there is no need to force the customer to pay more for water, which, by the way, does not even have a price on the menu. I had to get up to serve my wine because the bottle was far away and out of 4 waiters, none for 10 minutes were able to serve the wine. My husband went there and served. I gave up trying dessert. In short, excellent food, poor service and priceless water on the menu. Of all the 50 best that I visited, by far the worst service.

reviews.text: An amazing culinary adventure where the wait staff are your culinary expert and sommelier all in one. Décor is minimalistic but warm. Restaurant is cozy with less than 15 tables. Our BEST culinary experience in Lima

reviews.title: Unforgettable culinary experience in Lima
reviews.text: Renowned Lime culinary address, Merito will not have disappointed us! We tasted 5 steps away from 7 starters and main courses, before moving on to desserts. Each dish brings an explosion of flavors and sensations in the mouth, obtained by a successful fusion of Peruvian and Venezuelan cuisines! And each is preceded by a detailed explanation of its composition and how to taste it.

reviews.title: Haute cuisine at a reasonable price
reviews.text:
I started with pisco cocktail with cherimoya and we moved on to wine. The first thing we did was reserve the flan for dessert, just in case.
The dishes arrived without stress so that they were kept at their temperature. Very good fish with quinoa, shells, fish curry, lamb and sweetbreads. Oh, and the octopus. To repeat, without a doubt.
Very good service.

reviews.title: Deserves to be on the list of the 50 best in Latin America
reviews.text: I went to dinner with my husband to celebrate my birthday. Book way in advance (more than a week, at least), if there are more than 2 people. Beautiful place, with impeccably designed interior architecture and utensils. Excellent service and one of the best gastronomic experiences of our lives. Please try the flan!

reviews.title: A must go….
reviews.text: Our late lunch experience at this restaurant was truly exceptional, ranking among the top we've encountered worldwide. The chef's personal touch, guiding us through the culinary journey, added a special touch. The unique and thoughtful flavors, coupled with impeccable presentation, made it a remarkable and memorable gastronomic adventure.

reviews.title: Spectacular experience
reviews.text: This place was beyond amazing! From the location in old Barranco suburb to the old renovated building, the furniture, staff, food, drinks, everything was spectacular. The food was delicious! We loved what they have created at this small restaurant. Highly recommended! We hope to come back again one day!

reviews.title: Very good experience

reviews.title: Good food at a reasonable price
reviews.text:
We went out of the way to Barranco for a dinner at Mérito and it did not disappoint.

We had two main dishes, "oyster mushroom rice with asparragus and Andesino pesto", and "glazed pork belly with arepas". The rice dish was very good. The pork with arepas (corn dough stuffed with meat) was a bit cultue shock to me as a Chinese. We have something similar called roujiamo back at home. The pork belly was delicious, but I find it a bit difficult to eat it that way.

The dessert "corn and coffee cloud with lucuma and macambo" was very creative and delicious.

Service was a bit hit and miss. One gentleman was very nice. He explained the dishes very well and answered all my questions. Some other staff members were not proactive at all. I would expect better service for a restaurant ranked at 59 in the world.

We spent around US$30 per person, without any drinks. It was not cheap for Peru, but very reasonable compared to similar food back at home.

reviews.title: Inacceptable, rude, SLOW
reviews.text:
After 1 1/2 hours we had received one single starter, which was not harmonic in taste.

We were HUNGRY, asked when the other dishes should come. The waiter said ‚when they come, they come‘. Since the guests next table told us they were sitting already since 2 1/2 hours we asked for the bill.

When leaving we informed the owner why we‘re leaving and he just said ‚ok‘, no excuse, no explanation.

This restaurant is living for its previous reputation, the owner is trying to squeeze out of his reputation as much as he can.

reviews.title: Lovely lunch in Barranco district
reviews.text: Amazing Food, great atmosphere and very professional service. We loved it! We had lunch there (2 people) and had such a hard time deciding what to order as everything on the menu looked great. Our waiter helped us with clear recommendations and we were able to start by ordering a few starters and deciding on the go after that. We ended up splitting four starters and one main and one dessert. The dessert flan was spectacular!

reviews.title: Wonderful experience!
reviews.text: Fantastic experience! Food and service are top notch. The highlight was the grilled corn and pancetta. Also noteworthy are the drinks.

reviews.title: Perfect way to end our vacation
reviews.text:
Certainly the best restaurant we have been to even though we are used to Michelin-starred restaurants. The service is impeccable, the different dishes succulent, our taste buds were delighted.

To discover

reviews.title: Utterly delightful and sublime!
reviews.text:
If I could rate this restaurant with more than 5 stars, I would! A small, stylish and utterly delightful restaurant located in the upmarket area of Barranco. Reservations a must to secure a booking. The Chef Patron, Juan Luis Martinez and the team underneath him are geniuses. The restaurant is ranked 11th in South America and 59th in the world. Would not surprise me if it pushes even higher. 

Service is second to none - thoroughly professional, superbly trained and knowledgeable, polite and friendly. 

As for the food… I can describe this in one word: sublime! But I will use more. This restaurant provides a deep dive into Peruvian and South American cuisine, taking local dishes and elevating them to fine dining. Moreish and enlightening your taste buds. Devine. Memorable. Outstanding. 

We were just wowed. This sits there as one of the best restaurants we have ever eaten at. This is a perfect example of how food and service should be delivered. Bravo!

reviews.title: Tasting Merito
reviews.text: Excellent food, very nice experience, drinks are very good. Prices vs quality very well balanced. The pancetta was amazing, Negroni was very good!please order the “tostadas”

reviews.title: Friendly and cozy
reviews.text: The place is special. Small, charming and cozy. The kitchen is great. You don't force yourself to face a sequence of dishes. The menu features 9 starters, 5 main courses and 5 desserts. And you ask for what you want. The ideal is to order several dishes and share. All very good. Great wines by the glass. Worth the visit.

reviews.title: One of the best restaurants I've ever been to (so good I went twice)
reviews.text:
Potentially the best restaurant I've ever been to - would be 2 Michelin starred if Michelin covered Peru.

Sit at the Chef's counter if possible and order as many dishes as you can - especially the Fish Curry.

You have to book in advance - but always worth sending a Whatsapp on the day if it's last minute.

Can't recommend enough

reviews.title: Minimalist and powerful
reviews.text: Wonderful food and service, the portions are not large, but they are very tasty, the drinks are excellent, just the furniture is not very comfortable.

reviews.title: 'Disappointment after recognition
reviews.text:
We chose the 8 pm shift and I arrived before my wife. I stood outside until a waiter came out and asked: have they opened, YES are we already open? It was then that a woman came out asking if I had a reservation, I gave her the information and passed.
I greeted 10 people who were in the kitchen with a kind and necessary good night and only ONE person answered. I imagine the concentration when preparing your dishes required that degree of absence from external reality, so I got excited and thought: what good dishes await us.
Luis served us, very friendly and descriptive with the dishes, but he had no idea which dish to serve and/or offer first, which we paid for with a mix of hot and cold dishes that left a lot to miss, longing for Merito from when it wasn't award-winning that it was when we went up to 3 times and we always liked it. This time it was not the case. I don't know if the main chef is so worried about this recognition that he forgot the essential thing about his food: the flavor! and replaced it with the presentation. Thank you but we hope not to return soon

reviews.title: Elegantly rustic, exquisite, unique.
reviews.text:
As soon as you enter the place you are captivated by the decoration, it is like being inside a ruin, the tables according to the walls, the A1 tableware, the attentive service, the menu is not very varied, but each dish surprises you in the flavor, the presentation and quality of inputs.
They have natural infusions, signature cocktails and an interesting wine list, love the curved glasses without a base for the wine.
Prices according to the place.
Highly recommended.

reviews.title: Incredible experience
reviews.text: Exceptional! A must in Lima, the dinner experience in the kitchen is the best! All the preparation is very careful, the sweetbreads and the bacon arepas are the best!

reviews.title: Decent meal with international fusion
reviews.text: Came given all the great reviews but think it’s a bit overhyped. It’s decent but portion sizes are quite small and the flavors aren’t particularly special. It’s different from many other spots we’ve tried in Lima in that they use international flavors (some drinks were reminiscent of HK and the food had some Thai flavors), so I could see this being a good spot for locals / others living in Lima that are craving some non-Peruvian flavors, but if you’re a tourist and visiting, I wouldn’t recommend. For example, their pork dish basically tasted like a pork bun (except this had arepas) that you could get in many Chinese restaurants in NY. Their fish was a bit over cooked so it had a rubbery texture.

reviews.title: Meager Zen
reviews.text:
From passionatepalate

Meager Zen

Lima is a sprawling metropolis with an industrious twelve million of population blessed with a trading gene. Each Peruvian gives the impression of trying with diverse selling maneuvers and products to progress in the pursuit of attaining the next level within the orbit and hierarchy of enterprise. Lima is a zoo of traffic congested enthusiasts decidedly in formula one training.

Merito, this somewhat compressed diner, with a nondescript easily ignored façade is readily mimicked within as you penetrate directly into the kitchen. The first glance is the portrait of the seven cooking recruits all intent in the sublimation and brewing of the elements. You are spellbound witnessing the activity and shuffle of the ingredients. Merely the delicate scent of the spices becomes the catalyst that stirs the anticipation of feasting

Joan, the student of physics awaiting the doctorate, is temporarily director of alignment who accompanies you up the staircase to your dining abode. The decor is composed of sleek wooden surfaces that gently embraces you as you gaze at the starving Zen ambience which surrounds you. The atmosphere is set to calm.

The menu composition is either oceanic ( catch of the day) or meat-based (Beef cheeks or glazed pork belly).

We opted for the ocean sea bass curry style and fish accompanied by potato noodles.

The presentation of both dishes is obviously caressed by artistic input. The result is mesmerizing and the flaky flesh of fish bathing in a chili cream sauce imparts its delightful picante absolved of its picante with only residual flavor.  

The pastries are home grown with the similar artististic input that brags the external appearance of each dainty and soothes and sighs on ingestion. On the whole I am not the first nor the last to state the obvious: outstanding

This fine discovery is on a trajectory of testing new summits

Jean-Louis Bourque, Montreal, Quebec, Canada

reviews.title: Overrated
reviews.text: We booked here on a recommendation and based on reviews. It is rather overrated and seems to benefit from hype. The main courses are nothing special - they are not at all balanced. They are also very small and therefore overpriced. They were described as 'personal', but are more like small starters or tapas, though priced as a main. One was two small pieces of meat with two sauces and a scattering of tiny crisps. There was no vegetables or sufficient carbohydrates. No no side dishes are offered to create a more full meal. A choice of these should be offered within the price of each plate. The second main was too salty. Desserts were better; tasty and nicely presented, they offered slightly better value for money. Alcoholic drinks were too expensive and small. The menu does not sufficiently explain what any dish is, or what it comes with. One was simply translated as 'coconut'. The glowing reviews about incredible food just do not match what we encountered - it is perhaps more about saying you have been than it actually being fantastic. Overall, it is trying too hard and has a few too many gimmicks when good, balanced meals of reasonable size for a fair price would be better.

reviews.title: Amazing food
reviews.text:
I saw that Merito is one of the best restaurants to visit and I was not disappointed.  Every meal I had was amazing.  Every dish I tried was amazing!  I tried alot of dishes.

If on vacation do yourself a favor and order everything.  The waitress was very attentive amd gave great information on the dishes and how to eat the dishes.  

Definitely lives up to being one of the best restaurants in the world.

reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.text:
Exquisite food, unbeatable attention, very good small but cozy place, 
I will definitely return on my next visit to Peru.

reviews.title: BEST MEAL EVER
reviews.text:
I would give Merito 10 stars if I could. This was definitely one of the best meals in my life and I only came for lunch. We only tried 5 dishes but each was as good as the last. I will travel back to Lima only to eat here again. OMG

P.S. a word to the wise…eating at the chef’s table is a double edged sword. It is pure theater and the crew is super but you will have second thoughts about your order as you see everything cooked and plated. Bo need for second thoughts though because everything is delicious

reviews.title: Incredible!
reviews.text:
A beautiful lunch. This meal has really stayed with me. A lovely neighbourhood restaurant setting, though don’t be fooled as the food is world-class. Warm service made the whole experience a real memory of our time in Lima. 

The ‘Choclo a la brasa’ starter was deceptively simple at first sight, but delivers a flavour punch that felt quintessentially Peruvian. And I don’t think I’ll ever forget the fish curry which was recommended by our waiter. We topped it all off with the Chocolate Rock for dessert. Ah the chocolate rock - I’ll give anything to have that again! 

We’ve recommended Merito to anyone who will listen ever since. It is a must-visit.

reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.text: Amazing food and service, will definitely come back. This restaurant is a must if you are in Lima, food is delicious and staff is really friendly.

reviews.title: 💯 % good food food and Good atmosphere
reviews.text: Yummy Yummy Yummy !!! This is my best lunch in Lima and happy lunch , first u feel the nice service and second I see a handsome chef cooking in front me , all the dish is so delicious and good matching good presentation good looking that mean everything u eat is in a very nice taste , I am so so happy to eat and try the food , especially I have a good ending of dessert 🍮 super super delicious, u must go and try !!!!

reviews.title: Great food, service one notch behind - goos atmosphere, lots of locals
reviews.text: Went here twice on two visits to Lima.  Slightly off the beaten track but worth the walk.  Difficult to get in so book in advance.  Tapas style menu - things we tried were crab sandwiches, sea bass w artichoke,  scallops w panca chili and red potato chips, Octopus w beans (not my thing), sweetbreads (ug), goats cheese ice cream (wow), flan (like crème brûlée) - wow.  Waitress described dishes in Spanish even though she knew we didn’t speak Spanish and the service was not as good as the excellent food.

reviews.title: Arguably one of the best meals!
reviews.text: Arguably one of the best meals that I've had in Peru and we ate a lot of good food.  I made a reservation here before coming to Peru.  It is in a very cute neighborhood (Barranco).  When you go you almost feel like you are being ushered into a secret door.  The service was very good and the food was creative and delicious.  The space was beautiful and their plating was amazing.  I had a passionfruit drink that seemed to have hints of cinnamon, we had ceviche starters that were amazing and super flavorful and for my main I had the fish curry.  Everything was food happy dance worthy!

When you go you almost feel like you are being ushered into a secret door.  The service was very good and the food was creative and delicious.  The space was beautiful and their plating was amazing. reviews.title: Wonderful dinner.
reviews.text: Incredible service, food, and ambience - we loved dining at Merito and would definitely return again.  Highly recommend!

reviews.title: Great meal and experience at Merito
reviews.text: We loved our dinner at Merito in June 2022.  The courses were inventive, carefully prepared but not overly precious, and so tasty!  The meal is. thoughtful response to contemporary Latin dining,  For example, the cevice dish was the best we had in Lima.  The service was careful but not cloying.  And there was plenty of food (in contrast to the only concerns I've read). It was in fact a great value. This was the best meal of our eating trip to Lima.  Strongly recommended.

reviews.title: Eat here!!!
reviews.text: Omg food was soooo good, best we’ve had in Peru over three weeks. Cute, intimate setting and great service too. Love the corn starter (was like corn ribs) and have not stopped thinking about the choc rock dessert. Literally thinking of planning our flight out of Peru so we can go back throughLima for a night so I can eat the choc rock again. You should definitely eat here.

reviews.title: Wonderful meal and experience
reviews.text:
We came to Lima to eat and Merito was our best meal.  Wonderful vibe, with small dining rooms upstairs and hovering above the kitchen.  Each dish was creative without trying too hard, tasted terrific, and really shined a light on the ingredients.  
In a city with a lot of high end restaurants, Merito stand out.

reviews.title: Just RUN
reviews.text: We went to dine there with our family of 5. We ordered 6 dishes.  They all arrived tapas style but I’m talking about TINY dishes.  The dishes also arrived one at a time making us hangrier and hangrier as each dish arrived.  Some of them dishes literally arrived with two pieces of food on it.  The internet clearly did NOT give any indication as to how small the dishes were.  We are literally sitting here still at the dinner table trying to find another restaurant to have an actual dinner at.   If you are here on a date don’t expect the girl to say yes to a second date, if you’re here with your family they will think you’re not very bright for it reading this review.  The food wasn’t even worth taking a picture of…if you don’t believe this review without the pictures of every plate then you deserve to overpay for what will end up being appetizers to whatever you eat once you leave here.

reviews.title: OMG SO DELICIOUS!
reviews.text: We ate at a number of the Latin America's 50 Best Restaurants while in Lima and Merito deserves to be way higher on the list. The dishes are inventive, presented beautifully, and absolutely delicious. We were so blown away we wished we had time to go back so we could try more dishes. The decor is fabulous too. 100% you have to try this place!

reviews.title: One of the Best Meals I have had.
reviews.text:
This place is amazing. The food is out of this world. The freshness of the ingredients, the taste, and the presentations are all synced into perfect dishes. 
The Ambient is relaxed and welcoming and the service was superb.  I hope I get the opportunity to come back. This place is a Most for people visiting Lima.

reviews.title: Super friendly and easy-going gastronomic place in Barranco
reviews.text:
One of the best gastronomic experiences in Lima.
Although the street is rather noisy and not one of the cutest in the Barranco district, the place is definitely worth going.
You enter through the kitchen where you can see the cooks at work and go upstairs to find a nice minimalist deco restaurant.
We were a party of 5, ordered almost everything on the menu and shared all dishes among us.
Both cocktails and food are very creative and perfectly executed.
All fish dishes are wonderful, nicely spiced and perfectly cooked.
As for the desserts, the Flan is one of the best in my whole life, although it's more of a crème renversée than a proper Flan.

reviews.title: Fabulous food in a funky setting
reviews.text: Located in the heart of a buzzy area, Le Merito feels like a hidden secret. Coming off the street you are faced with a small but busy kitchen turning out delicious and tastebud-spinning and beautiful  plates for people seated in the single but elegant space above. The flavours they produce are fabulous and combine traditional Peruvian cuisine with influences from other countries and times. A feast for the senses!

reviews.title: I can eat here every day And not be bored!
reviews.text: very tasty food presented in fun ways. We were told they were small plates so we ordered five different plates and we were stuffed. Unfortunately, two full for dessert!

reviews.title: Hidden Gem in Lima
reviews.text: Merito was a little challenging to find in Lima, but the adventure was well worth it. Merito was a no-frills gastronomic experience! My girlfriend and I ordered multiple dishes, and all of them were delicious!  The food here was some of the best we ate in Lima.

reviews.title: without a doubt best quality_price relationship. Top food at reasonable price.
reviews.text: We went due to family recomendations and ended up concluding that is the second best experience of our gastronomical trip to lima and can easily achieve the top place in a couple of years.

reviews.title: Simply the best restaurant I did in 5 month in Colombia/Peru
reviews.text:
I went their twice, brought my family and girlfriend to make them taste the amazing food and cocktails of merito!
I m sure everything is amazing so I ll just give 2 recommandations.
The pulpo !! (Best I ever tasted )
The curry of paiche (huge amazonian fish that is just perfectly cooked )
They have around 30 cocktails so I m sure u ll find your taste and if you don t you can ask your special wish to the barman.
Thanks for the nights

reviews.title: Increíble
reviews.text: This was even better than our expectations. I highly recommend both the octopus and the rice confit. Both were among the best meals I’ve had in a month in Peru. The octopus was so tender, it was like it had been massages before being cooked. And the presentation was fantastic. Also the atmosphere and service were excellent. The plates and silverware are really cool. They also have stuff that works for vegan people!

reviews.title: Delicious!
reviews.text: The food was amazing and the service was friendly and welcoming! Perfect place for a solo traveler, duo or a group.

reviews.title: Amazing food , great atmosphere and deco . Very refreshing experience !
reviews.text: Amazing Food!!!! Very nice fusion , flavors , presentation of food very innovative . Location in Barranco district so trendy now a days . Calm and quiet , good protocols in place .

reviews.title: As always, Merito know exactly how to treat their clients. look forward to our next visit.
reviews.text: A business dinner with clients and colleagues went amazingly well, we had an area to ourselves, the food was delicious and the service was great.

reviews.title: Underwhelming
reviews.text:
I went to Mérito with the highest expectations as I had wanted to go since it opened and it had been highly recommended.  To begin, I will mention that the food was okay.  It was not great but it was not bad either.  It was nothing revolutionary.  Maybe revolutionary for Peru, since they don’t limit themselves to Peruvian flavors and Peruvian fusion and use Thai flavors and Venezuelan fusion but besides that, the food was  just ok.  

The real problem was the service and the attitude. 

The problem began when they took our drink orders.  First, they took more than 20 minutes to bring our cocktails even though we asked twice for them and the bar was nearly empty.  After they brought our drinks, they got one of the drinks wrong, and proceeded to argue with me about who was right.  After they left, they took another 15 minutes to bring the correct drink, at which point the dishes were already being served.  My drink actually arrived with our second dish. 

The timing of the dishes felt super rushed even though we told them that we were in no hurry. 

The next day when I checked the receipt (I didn’t check it carefully that night because we were rushed out because of the curfew, my bad), I noticed that I had been charged for the extra drink.   When I contacted the restaurant about it, of course they offered to refund the CC.  Obviously that has not happened yet.  

I understand that the pandemic has stressed the service industry particularly hard, which is why I still tipped a full 20% over the bill despite the bad service.  However, if Mérito is supposed to be one of the 50 Best Restaurants of Latin America, it should strive for very good service, especially as Peru re-opens it’s doors to tourists and welcomes them back.

reviews.title: Great choice
reviews.text: Nice environment, good food, a pleasant experience. Overall a great choice to have a nice night in Barranco.

reviews.title: Totally disrespects the clients!
reviews.text:
I recently went there for a dinner reservation. Arrived on time and started ordering some cocktails, all good. Received a very detailed explanation on the dishes which was really helpful and started ordering some things on the menu but asked not to bring them over still, as I was in no hurry at all (this was on a Saturday at 7 pm), and wanted to enjoy a few drinks before dinner. 

Accordingly, I ordered my second drink to the waitress and she nodded and walked away. I did noticed something weird in her attitude but decided to ignore her. A few minutes later came another waitress (a more “senior” one) and told me that they noticed I was asking for another drink but they wanted to start bringing over the food as they had another reservation coming over at 9:30 pm. It was only 7:45 pm. 

Lord knows it all went down from there. I should have just cancelled everything right then. Instead, I was polite enough and cancelled my second drink, and just let them bring the damn food over (flavors really good, some portions a bit small but ok, I get the concept). All in all, I was done by 8:30 pm (bill paid, no tip of course, as I do not condone this kind of behavior towards the customer).

If I were Merito’s owner, I would be really upset for having a couple of inexperienced people run my business without knowing that: 1. At a restaurant most profit margins come from alcoholic beverages (duh!) 2. They should avoid leaving an unattended table at a peak hour during the weekend for a whole 60 mins.

I felt absolutely mistreated and disrespected. I have been fortunate enough to dine at the world’s finest restaurants and I am no amateur, and this situation has never ever happened to me before, in places much more highly rated and with a much more higher status. Never coming back to this place, really disappointed. Avoid.

reviews.title: Service, a big fail, good food--now it does not matter
reviews.text: I had been picking my options to attend restaurants during the pandemic and this one looked like the one I can spend my few visits outside. We started with drinks, and we were visited constantly to pick the food. We pre-ordered to have more time for drinks until they came to say, you gotta order because we have a reservation at 9:30 pm. Of course, a couple of hours will be enough to have drinks and eat, but they were very desperate or looked like. We cut the last round of drinks, and ate, and left promptly at 8:30 pm, ONE HOUR BEFORE THEY NEEDED it to be cleared. I think that is really dumb since, although there is some other finance involved, if we kept drinking is better for them because there are always WAY BETTER margins on alcohol. I don't know what we event left them to serve the food. It was delicious, but the experience was already RUINED. Not coming back and definitely not recommending this place to locals or foreign visitors. You cannot do that to customers, you gotta manage your schedule and resources, and WE ALL KNOW there is a window of time, and WE AS CUSTOMERS always manage to keep our time to respect and share the space, no need to push that way.

reviews.title: Great food
reviews.text: Nice environment, great service, food was served in short time didn’t wait almost anything and we got good advice about what to order

reviews.title: What an experience!
reviews.text: The food was fantastic! We are a family of 4 including 2 teenagers, so I picked the a la carte option when making the reservation not wanting to lock my kids into the Nikkei experience with no choices. When we arrived, I asked if just I could do the Nikkei experience (the online reservation is all of nothing, not per person) and was told no, that it was only available by reservation. But, we were told we could do a 6 course meal, so 3 of us did that.  My husband had the short ribs that came with potatoes and rice and it was fantastic. The 6 course meal that my kids and I did proved to be a real experience and was great. Oddly enough, the last course was the entire short ribs meal my husband had, so that worked out that we got to have it as well since it was so good. I regularly found myself thinking that what I was eating tasted great, yet I had no idea what was in it and couldn't describe the flavor. It was just great! Service was also very good. Restaurant has no visible sign out front other than two plaques about it being rated in the top 50 restaurants in the world. We left stuffed and so happy we tried it.

reviews.title: Sublime
reviews.text: The food was sublime. The service was excellent. Best espresso martini I've ever had. Covid protocols not so good in the kitchen area.

reviews.title: excellent experience.
reviews.text: Amazing restaurant in a very cool neighborhood.  Creative and excellent ingredients.  Don’t miss visiting this restaurant .Service was excellent and attentive but friendly.  The food is very inventive with local ingredients and the drinks we’re excellent.  Don’t miss this restaurant

reviews.title: Exquisite food and outstanding service. Loved it!
reviews.text: I went there with my wife for our 14th anniversary, and the experience was superb. Friendly and diligent waitresses.

reviews.title: Excellent food!
reviews.text: We had a great time! The food was very good! So full of flavors and you can see the dedication that went into preparing the dishes.  We tried a couple different cocktails, they were high quality and hit the spot.  The staff were very accommodating and made us feel very welcoming!  We had run into the chefs gf Michelle at the restaurant, she too was extremely helpful in guiding us along the menu and giving recommendations for other restaurants in Lima that we ended up booking too.  You must check this place out, highly recommend it!

reviews.title: Lovely as always
reviews.text: For me this is one of the best restaurants in Lima. It’s warm atmosphere is matched by a great quality

reviews.title: Definitely worth a visit!
reviews.text: food is fresh, unextravagant yet exquisite and easy gentle on the palates. Natural wines make for a great pairing, for those who can appreciate the woody, flavorful, slightly sour aftertaste.

reviews.title: Amazing place!!!
reviews.text: The place is small but feels cozy. Everyone is very attentive and the food is amazing. On top of that, prices are good!! A favorite spot in lima!

reviews.title: Increadible vegetarian option !

Wow !!!

This was one of the best meals I've ever had. The food was unique, rich in flavor and texture, and super fresh. Everything had a clean, healthy feel. The plating and ingredients are gorgeous. The portions are generous. It's filling, yet light so you leave feeling great. 

And, what a treat to watch the chefs prepare the food in their open kitchen. Art in action!

reviews.title: Wow! Brilliant Venezuelan fusion. Bravo los inmigrantes!
reviews.text:
Small place which you barely notice from outside. 28 de Julio is noisy but once you are inside you dont notice.  Darkish wooden simple decor with a kitchen/counter eating downstairs and a few tables upstairs. Downstairs you get to watch the chefs.

The menu is small. 5 starters and 5 mains with a few deserts. There are links to Venezuela but the food is delicate and inventive, unlike anything you imagine from Vennie. Even the arepas are very light.
This is a place for sharing.  4 starters and two mains plus two deserts was enough for 4 people. Excellent yuca dish (dont think yuca, this is completely different). Delicious roasted corn with a dipping sauce. Mouth watering salad of "roots" and mushrooms. A chicken dish to die for. Excellent flan and chocolate deserts.  Good wine although not cheap. Overall about S./125 per head.

Lovely staff.  Only open evenings. If you dont book you can wait in bar nearby and they will call or come and fetch you when a table is free.

reviews.title: Amazing dinner / Delayed my flight to eat here again
reviews.text: Loved the atmosphere. The quesadilla and the corn were next level. Best quesadilla I have ever had, even in Mexico. Really loved the drinks. The coconut dessert was one of the best ones I have ever had. Went back for lunch. Set menu. Really amazing too and incredibly reasonably priced.

reviews.title: Wonderful food
reviews.text: I loved everything I tried. The octopus sent me into food heaven. Make sure you come before they open if you want to avoid the line of diners eager to feast on their very delicious food.

reviews.title: Wow!
reviews.text:
Wow! Fusion food that features the best of Venezuela and Perú? 

Oh my goodness, how can you go wrong! The food is perfect. Great flavors. Spectacular presentation. Awesome service. Wonderful wine pours and bespoken cocktails. It’s the perfect package.

Okay, it’s a tiny spot with little room to stretch your elbows. But, that’s a near minor inconvenience. The food melds so delightfully to the foodie cultures of Perú and Venezuela - it gives both countries a clear path to their culinary expertise. 

I highly recommend this tiny Barranco spot for a lovely evening of gastronomic delights.

reviews.title: One of the best !
reviews.text: This is one of the best restaurants that we have been to, and we have travelled all over the world ! Outward appearance is low key & chic. Excellent and knowledgeable service, and then the food arrives ... sensational !!! We had octopus & the spare rib, choc rock for dessert. A little expensive but well and truly worth the experience. Enjoy !

reviews.title: One of the best restaurants I’ve ever visited.
reviews.text:
INCREDIBLE. 

There are no words to describe just how good Merito is. Every dish we tried was fantastic.

reviews.title: Unique and Delicious Food
reviews.text:
Amazing and different Venezuelan and Peruvian food. The pork arepas are the best I’ve ever had. The hot vegan ceviche (mushrooms, corn, and other veggies) was delicious and so satisfying that we didn’t even miss the seafood. We also seriously considered licking the bowl. Don’t forget to save room for dessert. 

As a caution, they don’t have an English menu, since the restaurant is more of a local favorite than a tourist spot, and the staff do not speak a lot of English. However, the waiters are super helpful and patient and explained what the menu items were in slow Spanish to us. The prices are also very reasonable considering the high quality of the ingredients and the exquisite preparation.

reviews.title: Excellent from Start to Finish
reviews.text: Merits is an amazing restaurant that is not overrun with tourists and visited by locals. We were tipped off to Merito by locals and loved our entire dining experience here. Since we had a late lunch we went with more starters and ended on dessert. The octopus, corn, gyoza and quesadilla were all phenomenal. We ended with getting the chocolate rock and chiromoya three ways. The rock alone from a presentation perspective is worth it. Highly recommend this place. We didn’t have any reservations we walked in early (Lima early) at 7:30 and were seated right away.

reviews.title: Pricey but unique and tasty experience!
reviews.text: El Mérito has exceptional food! Although the food is pricey (between 20-60 soles per appetizer, $6-17) the experience is worth every sol! I sat at the bar which was a great way to see the food being prepared right in front of you. I was also able to chat with the 2 main chefs which is a rare opportunity in most restaurants of this calibre. They even let me hang around until closing to enjoy the atmosphere. I ordered the choclo and the pulpo (octopus) and both were amazing, resembling plates from the world famous Peruvian restaurant Central.  Highly recommend for a special night out!

reviews.title: Creative place with delicious food
reviews.text: We had a really nice experience at Merito, which serves a fusion between venezuelan and peruvian food! The staff is friendly and informative and the dishes where interesting and delicious. We where 6 people, 3 of us vegetarian. This is a place where most dishes are ment to shared, so we shared among veggies and non veggies. The non vegetarians had the octopus, fish arepas and choclo. Veggies had choclo, green sallad, mushroom sallad and arepas. Everything was beautifully presented and delicious! The choclo dish was a real favourit for everyone, so simple but completely amazing! We also tried different kinds of non alcoholic infusions which where great, as well as really nice coffee. Would not miss a visit to this place when in Barranco!

reviews.title: Peruvian cuisine on steroids!
reviews.text: We visited Merito as part of a “gastro  tour” with our amazing guide Gabriel. If you’re lucky enough to get a seat overlooking the kitchen, you’re in for an amazing experience... Nothing quite compares to watching Merito’s culinary  “artists” meticulously create an array dishes which are as delicious as they are beautiful. We tried their roasted corn, fish tartar, goat cheese quesadilla and grilled fish arepas - all served with unique and flavorful sauces of peppers and other herbs and vegetables. For dessert we had a baked chirimoya (tastes somewhat similar to apple or pear) with ice cream and shaved ice. Altogether a spectacular experience!!

reviews.title: Great for small groups
reviews.text: I visited Merito as part of a girls’ night out and really enjoyed the Peruvian- Venezuelan food. The menu is very small but includes various vegetarian options so that probably won me over. As a group of 4, we tried most things on the menu and all dishes were enjoyed. The wine list is also tiny but I was happy with the Prosecco on hand. My only complaint is that the location is small and they don’t take bookings nor do they have a waiting area, which meant we had to wait more than an hour for a table at another location. Fortunately it’s a couple of doors up from Barra 55 so that’s a great option for a pre-dinner drink or two as you wait, and you can send someone from your party to keep checking on the table, as Merito will not call you when your table is ready nor accept phone calls from you to check. Were Merito to change their policy on bookings or phone calls I would definitely score them higher as I loved the place regardless of the inconvenience they caused my group. Please do check them out, but go when you’re relaxed and ready to wait!

reviews.text: Merito Restaurant in Barranco (Lima) is a true hole in the wall that hits you with a powerful savory punch with their assortment of dishes.  Venezuelan chefs Juan Luis Martínez y José Luis Saumeo are dealing with a very sophisticated culinary crowd in Lima and they deliver.  Juan Luis worked for two years as a chef at La Central Restaurant in Lima which is considered one of the top 10 restaurants in the word and it shows.  The service, the presentation and the quality of the cuisine are a reflection of a highly trained team. The superb quality of culinary options in Lima keeps growing. No surprise that Peru for the 7th year in the row is considered the best culinary destination in the world.

reviews.title: For those who want Central with no reservations
reviews.text:
Headed by a Sous chef from Central (just 2 blocks away), this was mind blowing. Perhaps the best Octopus I've had in 2 years. I'm not quite sure how they cooked it so that the outside was gelatinous, the inside firm and suckers charred and crispy, all at the same time. Magnificent.

The panceta and arepas asado reminded me of Chinese pork buns but...distinctly Peruvian. Another fantastic riff on classic flavor profiles bound to delight. 

This is the perfect place for those who want the ingenuity and flavor packed profile of Central but could not score a reservation or do not wish to ingest a 12 course, 3 hour long meal.

reviews.title: this really is the business
reviews.text: If you're not too fussed about your surroundings, love tasty, different and well presented food, and prefer not to spend a fortune then head for Merito. Slightly odd location a block and a bit from the main Barranco piazza, there are a few stools at the bar where dishes are prepared downstairs and some more seating with comfortable tables and benches/chairs upstairs (the adobe bricks give that area a slightly distressed look offset by the well chosen furnishings). The menu is short but very appetising with a mixture of Peruvian and Venezuelan elements (roast choclo/corn on one side, arepas on the other with fried yuca in between), and all the starters and mains we tried had interesting vegetables/sauces. There wasn't a dud among our choices and some outstanding offerings including the scallop/squid, the roast fish (cabrillo), and the sepas with (among other things) black radishes. Despite being replete all dishes were wiped clean and there was still room to try the a couple of the desserts (there are only three) with the roca de chocolate being the winner by a head. Apart from regular Pilsen, two artesan beers (one wheat based but clear) are available as well as half a dozen wines. The coffee is excellent if you like it strong. Service is first rate - knowledgeable, friendly and efficient. And the prices ? Extremely good value for food this interesting and of this quality (90 soles per head excluding service but including an alcoholic beer each). Go now before the place gets too popular !
